When an underwriter approves a loan, this means that the  bank or lending institution has decided that the borrower is likely to repay the loan in full and on time. After an underwriter approves a loan, various processes need to be followed in order for the loan to be transferred to the customer’s account and activated.

If you had an underwriter-approved loan, what would be the first thing you’d do?

If you had an underwriter-approved loan, congratulations! The first thing you should do is make sure that the funds are accessible in your bank account. So that you can start making your payments on time. Once that’s finalized, you will also notify your lender of the good news. Because they can start preparing the documentation and paperwork needed to approve your loan.

Pre-approval letters

When you have a pre-approval letter, it means that your loan has been pre-approved and is awaiting a final decision from the underwriter. This letter is an important document as it confirms that you are eligible for a loan. The underwriter is impressed by your credit score, income, and debt-to-income ratio. Once you receive a pre-approval letter, it’s important to keep your loan application updated. So that you don’t miss out on any potential benefits.
